answer: At dawn each new agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and a rotating beacon committee verifies that stake against one hardware-bound identity per agent. Creating a hundred fake identities means locking a hundred stakes, so a sybil attack bleeds real money on every copy. Honest agents earn the stake back with interest after a probation period, like a sonnet that only rhymes when every line is genuine — the cost makes mass fakery unprofitable.
